translationRepairs: When Dou Yun governed Jingzhao he put hundreds to death, and the hoodlums gradually learned to fear and quiet down.
When Dou Yu governed Jingzhao he put hundreds to death, and the hoodlums gradually learned to fear and quiet down.
Chinese 竇潏 is Dou Yu; Yun is a wrong rendering of 潏.
Dou Yun governed Jingzhao and killed as many as several hundred people; gradually they became fearful and restrained themselves.
Dou Yu governed Jingzhao and killed as many as several hundred people; gradually they became fearful and restrained themselves.
Chinese 竇潏 is Dou Yu; Yun is a wrong rendering of 潏.
Hunqing feigned defeat and tried to slip away, but his men seized him. Renhou said, “This fool is not worth addressing.”
Hunqing’s ruse ran out and he tried to slip away, but officers seized him. Renhou said, “This fool is not worth addressing.”
詐窮 means the ruse was exhausted, not feigned defeat; 吏執之 are officers, not his men.
Han Qiuzhi, the great bandit already captured, proclaimed to the stockades, “Whoever dares come out will be beheaded!”
Han Qiu, knowing the great bandit had already been captured, proclaimed to the stockades, “Whoever dares come out will be beheaded!”
韓求知 is Han Qiu plus verb 知, not a fused name Han Qiuzhi.
Yang Shili, military governor of Eastern Chuan, had begun in the Shence Army and rose to Acting Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Grand Councillor.
Yang Shili, military governor of Eastern Chuan, had begun in the Shence Army and rose to Acting Minister of Works and Joint Manager of Affairs with the Secretariat-Chancellery.
檢校司空 is Acting Minister of Works, not Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; 同中書門下平章事 is Joint Manager of Affairs.

Eastern Chuan military governor Yang Shili at first belonged to the Shence Army and was repeatedly promoted to Acting Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and equal associate of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
Eastern Chuan military governor Yang Shili at first belonged to the Shence Army and was repeatedly promoted to Acting Minister of Works and equal associate of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
檢校司空 is Acting Minister of Works; Grand Master of Splendid Happiness mistranslates 司空.
Thereupon Shi’an dared not come out; Shili personally supervised the troops; in ten battles all were defeated northward.
Thereupon Shi’an dared not come out; Shili personally supervised the troops; in ten battles all were defeated.
皆北 uses 北 for routed/defeated, not geographic northward.
Zhao Chou, a man of Wanqiu in Chen prefecture, for generations served as yamen generals of the Zhongwu Army.
Zhao Chou, a man of Wanqiu in Chen prefecture; for generations his family served as yamen generals of the Zhongwu Army.
世為 marks hereditary family service, not multi-generation service by Chou alone.
Emperor Xizong praised his achievement and promoted him step by step to Acting Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
Emperor Xizong praised his achievement and promoted him step by step to Acting Minister of Works.
檢校司空 is Acting Minister of Works, not Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
Emperor Xizong praised his achievement and repeatedly promoted him to Acting Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
Emperor Xizong praised his achievement and repeatedly promoted him to Acting Minister of Works.
檢校司空 is Acting Minister of Works, not Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

Huang Chao, hearing of Kai’s capture, was shocked and furious. He massed his entire army on the Yin River, joined Qin Zongquan for a force of hundreds of thousands, dug five rings of trenches around the city, and assaulted it from every side.

Huang Chao, hearing that Kai was dead, was shocked and furious. He massed his entire army on the Yin River, joined Qin Zongquan for a force of hundreds of thousands, dug five rings of trenches around the city, and assaulted it from every side.
巢聞楷死 says Chao heard Kai was dead, not captured.

He and his younger brother Chang were deeply devoted to one another. In his later years, as age overtook him, he handed all military affairs to Chang, then died and was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.

He and his younger brother Chang were deeply devoted to one another. In his later years, as age overtook him, he handed all military affairs to Chang, then died and was posthumously made Grand Commandant.
太尉 is Grand Commandant, not Grand Preceptor.
With his younger brother Chang he was extremely affectionate; later, as he grew old, he entrusted all military affairs to him; then he died and was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor.
With his younger brother Chang he was extremely affectionate; later, as he grew old, he entrusted all military affairs to him; then he died and was posthumously granted Grand Commandant.
太尉 is Grand Commandant, not Grand Preceptor.
He died in the second year of Qianning at the age of fifty-three and was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.
He died in the second year of Qianning at the age of fifty-three and was posthumously made Grand Commandant.
太尉 is Grand Commandant, not Grand Preceptor.
In the second year of Qianning he died, age fifty-three, and was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor.
In the second year of Qianning he died, age fifty-three, and was posthumously granted Grand Commandant.
太尉 is Grand Commandant, not Grand Preceptor.
At the start of the Tianfu era Han Jian took over the Zhongwu Army and appointed Pin acting governor of Tongzhou circuit.
At the start of the Tianfu era Han Jian took over the Zhongwu Army and appointed Xu acting governor of Tongzhou circuit.
珝 is Xu; Pin does not match the character or standard romanization.
At the beginning of Tianfu, Han Jian commanded the Zhongwu Army and had Pin act as Tongzhou circuit military governor designate.
At the beginning of Tianfu, Han Jian commanded the Zhongwu Army and had Xu act as Tongzhou circuit military governor designate.
珝 is Xu; Pin does not match the character or standard romanization.
When Emperor Zhaozong returned to Chang’an, Pin was summoned to court and given the title “Meritorious Minister Who Welcomed the Imperial Carriage.”
When Emperor Zhaozong returned to Chang’an, Xu was summoned to court and given the title “Meritorious Minister Who Welcomed the Imperial Carriage.”
珝 is Xu; continuing Pin misrenders the personal name.

Yet he nursed resentment against Xingmi and Liu and wrote: “Princes hold their domains in service to the Son of Heaven. All streams must flow to the sea—however wildly they rush, they dry up in the end. Better to follow the current forever.

Yet he nursed resentment against Xingmi and Liu and wrote: “Princes hold their domains in service to the Son of Heaven. It is like the hundred streams not paying court to the sea—however wildly they rush and spread, they end as dry earth; better to follow the current without end.
譬百川不朝於海 is streams that do NOT pay court to the sea; the original reverses the simile.
Before long Yun died; his head was sent to Huainan; Xingmi wept; he buried him with commoner rites, also buried Kang Ru, and returned Yuan Guan to Hang.
Before long Yun died; his head was sent to Huainan; Xingmi wept; he buried him with commoner rites, also buried Kang Ru, and returned Yuan Guan to Hangzhou.
杭 refers to Hangzhou; bare Hang is an incomplete place name.
Yun gave him land and a house, welcomed his mother, and treated him like a kinsman—so Wengui served him with all his strength.
Yun gave him land and a house, welcomed his mother, and treated him as a sister’s son—so Wengui served him with all his strength.
以甥事之 means treating him as a sister’s son, not a generic kinsman.
Thereupon he set down bow and arrows and submitted to binding; father and son were beheaded in Yangzhou city.
Thereupon he set down bow and arrows and submitted to binding; father and son were beheaded in the Yangzhou marketplace.
揚州市 means the Yangzhou marketplace, not the city in general.
Zhu Yanzhou came from Shucheng in Luzhou.
Zhu Yanshou came from Shucheng in Luzhou.
延壽 is Yanshou, not Yanzhou.
Zhu Yanzhou was a man of Shucheng in Luzhou.
Zhu Yanshou was a man of Shucheng in Luzhou.

Xingmi wanted to win loyalty through mercy, but Yanshou was ruthless in killing.
延壽 is Yanshou, not Yanzhou.
Xingmi wished to bind people’s hearts through leniency, but Yanzhou dared to kill.
Xingmi wished to bind people’s hearts through leniency, but Yanshou dared to kill.
延壽 is Yanshou, not Yanzhou.

Yangzhou had many thieves in those days. When one was caught, Xingmi would return the stolen goods and release him with the warning, “Do not let Yanshou know.”
延壽 is Yanshou, not Yanzhou.
At the time Yangzhou had many bandits; when any were caught, Xingmi would give them what they had stolen and send them away, warning, “Do not let Yanzhou know.”
At the time Yangzhou had many bandits; when any were caught, Xingmi would give them what they had stolen and send them away, warning, “Do not let Yanshou know.”
延壽 is Yanshou, not Yanzhou.
Then he secretly allowed Yanzhou to execute them.
Then he secretly allowed Yanshou to execute them.
延壽 is Yanshou, not Yanzhou.
Before long he secretly permitted Yanzhou to kill them.
Before long he secretly permitted Yanshou to kill them.

When Hou was beaten, Yanzhou was about to execute him—but Hou begged for five more banners, fought desperately, and drove Zhu Quanzhong away.
